item.title: The mutational landscape of STING-induced immunity
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 24 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10685-3

A massively parallel assay systematically charts the sequence-function landscape of the STING signalling protein, and the findings define molecular principles that tune STING activity and show its functional potential across immune contexts.

item.title: Genetic technologies to enhance crop nutritional value under climate change
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 24 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10593-6

This Review reflects on the joint power of genetic technologies, including untapped CRISPR–Cas techniques to combat hidden hunger and improve crop resilience, and argues in favour of their combined use to overcome these societal challenges.

item.title: Dietary cholesterol activates a Ral-dependent pathway driving LDLR turnover
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 24 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10697-z

Chronic dietary cholesterol activates Ral GTPases, which promote LDLR internalization and lysosomal degradation through RalBP1–REPS1 and CTSA, thereby reducing cholesterol clearance, whereas CTSA inhibition restores LDLR function and may offer a therapeutic strategy for cardiovascular disease.

item.title: Global high-resolution mapping of seagrass to support conservation
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 24 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10704-3

Global high-resolution mapping shows widespread seagrass loss and degradation since 2019, with most meadows outside protected areas, highlighting urgent conservation and climate-policy needs.

item.title: Disparate privacy risks from medical AI
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 24 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10688-0

AI models for medical diagnostics are vulnerable to membership inference attacks.

item.title: Small-molecule modulation of β-arrestins
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 24 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10683-5

Integrated pharmacological, biochemical, biophysical and structural analyses of small-molecule β-arrestin inhibitors show how they block β-arrestin engagement with activated GPCRs, revealing their mechanism of action and uncovering a previously unrecognized allosteric regulatory site.

item.title: Immunological mechanisms of mRNA vaccines for infectious diseases
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 24 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10599-0

A Review of the immunological mechanisms of mRNA–lipid-nanoparticle vaccines for infectious diseases discusses how the components of this vaccine platform can be modified to fine-tune immune responses against challenging pathogens.

item.title: Optical cooling by interfacial charge transfer in 2D heterostructures
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 24 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10662-w

Optical cooling in two-dimensional semiconductor heterostructures is demonstrated through phonon-assisted interfacial charge transfer, enabling cryogen-free thermal management without stringent quantum-efficiency requirements.

item.title: Detection of anisotropic cosmic structures on a gigaparsec scale
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 24 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10702-5

Using the parameter-free Angular Distribution of Pairwise Distances for measuring directional correlations, evidence is found for coherent anisotropic structures extending over gigaparsec scales, challenging the assumption that the Universe becomes statistically isotropic on sufficiently large scales.

item.title: An ECG biomarker for sudden cardiac death discovered with deep learning
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 24 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10674-6

A deep-learning model trained on electrocardiogram (ECG) waveforms identifies an easily visible biomarker that predicts sudden cardiac death more accurately than the current clinical state of the art.

item.title: Epiblast diversification and blood formation in a human pregastrula
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 24 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10698-y

High-resolution spatial transcriptome analysis of a human embryo at Carnegie stage 6 reveals three distinct developmental trajectories from the epiblast towards amnion, primitive streak and axial mesoderm, and detects the initiation of haematopoiesis before gastrulation, originating from hypoblast rather than epiblast.

item.title: Fourier pixels for bidirectional light control
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 24 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10681-7

A versatile platform of miniaturized Fourier-optics-based diffractive elements enables multifunctional pixels that fully control and sense the amplitude, phase and polarization of optical wavefronts for advanced photonic applications.

item.title: Genetic diversity of late Neanderthals in northwestern Europe
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 24 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10625-1

Genetic sequencing of multiple late Neanderthals living less than 52,500 years ago provides an overview of genetic diversity and demonstrates that even low-coverage nuclear genome data can increase resolution of within-Neanderthal diversity.

item.title: Crude oil fractionation by means of mesoporous polyacrylonitrile membranes
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 24 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10677-3

Porous polyacrylonitrile membranes—typically used as non-selective support layers—can be used to achieve effective molecular refining of crude oil at steady state, enabling substantial reductions in energy consumption, cooling water, and CO2 emissions compared with distillation processes.

item.title: GW250114 reveals signatures of post-merger black-hole horizon
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 24 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10696-0

The observation of a direct wave after the merger of two black holes reveals signatures associated with the remnant black-hole horizon, establishing an observational channel to directly measure frame-dragging effects in black-hole ergospheres and probe the horizon surface gravity.

item.title: Chiral laser gyroscopes breaking the lock-in limit
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 24 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10684-4

Ring laser gyroscope lock-in has been eliminated using spontaneous symmetry breaking in a He–Ne laser, enabling accurate near-zero rotation sensing without external components, improving miniaturization and precision.

item.title: Zero-shot design of drug-binding proteins via neural iterative selection−expansion
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 24 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10670-w

By pairing two neural networks in an iterative optimization algorithm, small-molecule binding proteins can be designed from scratch with high accuracy, affinity and success rates, showing promise for applications in drug delivery and sequestration.

item.title: Ductile alloys offering 100 MPa tensile strength at 2,400 °C
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 24 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10708-z

A boron-stabilized oxide-strengthened tantalum alloy combines exceptional room-temperature ductility with record ultrahigh-temperature strength, enabling load-bearing applications above 2,000 °C.

item.title: Alternate RNA decoding results in stable and abundant proteins in mammals
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 24 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10678-2

Alternate RNA decoding, an understudied process, leads to peptide sequence modifications that can have substantial functional effects on protein stability, tissue-specific proteomes and disease.

item.title: A Streptomyces megacluster encodes synergistic biotin-targeting antibiotics
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 24 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10647-9

In Streptomyces spp., a conserved biosynthetic gene megacluster produces an arsenal of distinct antimicrobials that converge on bacterial biotin biosynthesis as a naturally evolved combination therapy.

item.title: Laser light switches on heat flow in ultra-thin structures
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 24 June 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-01803-2

A temperature difference of more than 100 kelvin can be created between stacked layers of 2D material by irradiating them with laser light.

item.title: Genomic insights into the population dynamics and demise of Neanderthals
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 24 June 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-01704-4

A surge of genetic data from the skeletal remains of Neanderthals disproves some assumptions and generates fresh questions about these ancient hominins.

item.title: A hidden predictor of sudden cardiac death uncovered by deep learning
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 24 June 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-01806-z

A machine-learning model trained on thousands of electrocardiogram recordings identifies a previously unrecognized group of at-risk people.

item.title: ‘Megacluster’ of genes enables bacteria to make potent antibiotic mixture
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 24 June 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-01804-1

Soil bacteria make cocktails of molecules that synergistically inhibit the growth of microbial pathogens — suggesting a strategy for tackling antibiotic-resistant infections.

item.title: Antibiotic cocktail made by soil bacteria can kill superbugs
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 24 June 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-01990-y

Four antibiotic compounds produced in Streptomyces bacteria attack multiple parts of an essential metabolic pathway.

item.title: Crude oil turns cheap porous membrane into a sieve to refine itself without heat
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 24 June 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-01896-9

An inexpensive, porous polymer membrane helps to separate raw crude oil, without heat or selective coating. Heavy hydrocarbons self-assemble inside the pores to create channels that are likely to be less than 2 nanometres wide, enriching the resulting permeate mix into light, ‘naphtha range’ hydrocarbons with 30% less energy cost and carbon dioxide emissions than conventional distillation.

item.title: Long-sought chemical inhibitors of β-arrestin proteins
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 24 June 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-01894-x

Proteins called β-arrestins regulate signalling through members of the G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) superfamily. Small molecules that bind directly to the β-arrestins and inhibit their activities are the first chemical tools to probe their biology, opening avenues for transducer-targeted, pathway-specific GPCR therapeutics.

item.title: A global map of seagrass ecosystems
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 24 June 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-01805-0

Combining satellite imagery and machine learning has created the first comprehensive map of seagrass meadows, in a boost for the conservation of these crucial ecosystems.

item.title: AI tool spots antibiotics that fight drug-resistant gonorrhoea
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 24 June 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-01987-7

The bacterium Neisseria gonorrhoeae has evolved resistance to most antibiotics used to treat it, but a machine-learning screen reveals potential therapies.

item.title: Volcanic magma sculpts eerie domes on the sea floor
item.description:
Nature, Published online: 24 June 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-01986-8

Carbon dioxide bubbling up from underground material can solidify into formations of up to five metres tall.
